reviews.title: Still needs tons of improvement on desktop
reviews.text:
I really love this app on mobile, but on desktop it’s much harder to do what I do on my phone.

I can’t delete lists on the desktop app, and the emojis glitch in the calendar day view, so it’s hard to see which part of the day you’re in.

I use this app a lot in both my personal and professional life because it makes it easy to see how the day is going and to move activities around. For work, though, it’s not ideal, because the Mac app is much weaker than the iPhone one. Because of that, I have to use the browser, and I can’t keep my work activities up to date easily. My job requires me to have hundreds of tabs open, so I lose track of the app’s tab and of what I need to do. Some days I end up going back to a notepad to remember my tasks, which defeats the main purpose of the app: helping people with ADHD.

Technically, on Mac it’s just one more app for listing tasks, not one that actually helps with ADHD.

reviews.title: What happened to the confetti???
reviews.text:
Update: one of the things I liked most about this app was the little celebratory confetti effect when I marked a task completed. It was an acknowledgment of effort and helped me stay motivated to keep working towards completing my tasks. Now it’s gone and Tiimo has gone from being genuinely useful to me, and being recommended to others by me, to something utilitarian that can easily be replaced with Apple’s built in reminders App. I’m very disappointed.

I’ve found this app to be helpful in keeping me focused on the things I want to accomplish. I know that it has more capability than I utilize, but I simply don’t need all of it. I do have one complaint and that’s with the frequent push for users to upgrade to premium. I’ve gotten pop ups every time I open the app this week encouraging me to take advantage of a premium subscription discount. It’s very frustrating to have my concentration disrupted by a sales pitch before I’m allowed to add a task. Now, with this most recent update, the option to choose an emoji symbol relevant to my task has been moved behind the premium pay wall. 

I understand that the developers are in business to turn a profit, but the tactic of gradually eliminating functionality feels disingenuous. If it continues, free account users will either feel forced to pay, or give up on the app altogether. I sincerely hope it won’t come to that for me.

reviews.title: Beautiful design, but frustrating to use
reviews.text:
I’ve had a Tiimo subscription for two years, and I genuinely like the design and visual approach of the app. Unfortunately, I keep running into the same problem: there’s so much friction involved in creating, editing, and rescheduling tasks that I eventually stop using it after a few weeks.

Ironically, for me, it’s one of the least ADHD-friendly planners I’ve tried. A planner should reduce the mental effort required to organize my day, not become another task I have to manage.

I’ve also given the AI assistant several chances, but so far it’s been more of a waste of time than a helpful feature. For example, I gave it a simple instruction to schedule my work shifts for next week, from 16:00 to midnight, with Tuesday and Thursday off. It initially scheduled me for all seven days, and I had to repeatedly clarify the instructions and specify exact dates to prevent it from changing other weeks.

By the time the AI finally understands what I want, I’ve spent more time explaining and correcting it than it would have taken to enter everything manually.

I really want to love Tiimo because the visual design is excellent. But the functionality needs to be much more intuitive, flexible, and reliable. For an ADHD planner, reducing friction should be the number one priority.

You know, the more expensive option that you're also conveniently most likely to forget about. And of course the only way to get the free trial is the annual plan. If you're not familiar with this manipulation tactic, you might not notice that you can just use the free version of the app by pressing the 'x' in the corner. (I have been tricked by this in the past so I don't think it's unreasonable to call it manipulative design for people with adhd). Not to mention the "one-time only offer" for 50% off an annual plan! reviews.title: Requires more effort than it helps.
reviews.text:
AI planner is awful, often giving inaccurate timings (you tell it that you need to do a task before midday, and it schedules it for 12:15) and needing amending, but only lets you accept or reject all of the actions it presents, rather than selecting which ones it got right or wrong. 

Manually inputting reminders is tedious and there is no separation between early and late afternoon. 

It also really pushes you to upgrade to premium (as soon as you open the app, what feels like every single time) which can interrupt your train of thought or when you want to note something down before you forget. 

The homescreen widgets add little to no useful functionality, and have a massive “upgrade to premium” badge. 

For an app designed to help you plan and declutter your brain, it sure does require a lot of micromanagement. 

To be honest the default iOS calendar and reminder apps are far more intuitive and do everything you’d need.

You also can only accept or reject its actions, you can’t correct them to tell the LLM what was wrong when the only issue is the time or a misheard word. For example, I said I needed to pick something up on the way home from an appointment, so it scheduled that reminder for 90min after the appointment ended instead of at the end time, but that was so many taps to correct it wasn’t really worth using the AI to begin with. It is not remotely capable of transforming a nebulous description of chores into actionable, scheduled steps, despite basically putting that ability on the tin. It’s really just a purpose built Siri focused only on reminders, and it can do a whole lot less than Siri. Add to that the UI is just plain confusing and unintuitive, things are divided into tabs in the most useless way, and none of the top level tabs feel as useful as they should be. This app feels like work to use when it’s supposed to make things easier.

reviews.title: Felt very exploitative. Instant delete.
reviews.text:
Before I could even see the app, I was shown a subscription screen. I tapped the X because I wanted to explore the product before paying. Instead of taking me to the app, it presented another sales screen stating: “This offer only appears once. Grab 40% off before it’s gone.”

I found this use of artificial urgency very exploitative. It pressures users to make an immediate purchasing decision before they can evaluate what they are buying. This is particularly troubling in an ADHD-focused app, since ADHD can involve impulsivity and difficulty making decisions under pressure.

The very next screen prompted me to rate the app, although I still had not seen or used it. That screen also advertised “Over 30,000 five-star reviews.” Requesting ratings before users have experienced the product undermines their credibility and makes me question how meaningful those reviews are.

An app claiming to support people with ADHD should hold itself to a much higher ethical standard. I deleted it immediately.

reviews.title: Too confusing to be useful
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like this app, especially since it’s marketed toward people with ADHD, but my experience has been frustrating.

The biggest issue is performance. Even on desktop, the app lags a lot, which makes it harder to stay focused instead of helping.

More importantly, the structure is confusing. There are multiple overlapping features like to-do lists, daily lists, schedules, and options to create additional lists. Instead of simplifying planning, it adds layers that feel overwhelming.

The AI features also don’t seem reliable. It sometimes creates duplicate categories instead of recognizing ones that already exist, which just adds more clutter.

reviews.title: NOT for ADHD brain, wasted so much time trying to set up
reviews.text: Not good for this ADHD brain! I wanted to use this to schedule tasks and keep from getting sidetracked, but instead I’m practically in tears after wasting over an hour trying to set up my schedule. I used the AI “Co-Planner” and spoke out what I need to get done today, and it did add everything to my task list but didn’t suggest specific time slots as I had expected. I tried using the Co-Planner to edit and add time slots to all of the tasks (plan my day for me, as I thought this app was supposed to do), but it says I don’t have anything planned! I asked it to change the time of a scheduled task and it asks for the title of the task, then says it can’t find the task! The only way to change anything is to manually go into each task and update the time/duration, which I already have the option to do on my calendar app FOR FREE! The AI feature is also super slow on both PC and iPhone, and it stopped responding completely when I tried using it on my phone. Visually, I can see it being useful IF and ONLY IF it were easier to set up a schedule in the first place. I’m really disappointed in all of the ADHD/AuDHD influencers out there who have recommended this app and I feel like the good reviews have to be phony. I can’t see how anyone with a neurodivergent brain could honestly say this app helped them, unless they have someone else doing the setup and scheduling. Now I’ve wasted even more time writing this review so others with a brain like mine don’t suffer the same fate!

reviews.title: Tolle Ideen, schlechte Umsetzung
reviews.text:
Ich durfte Tiimo nun für ein paar Tage kostenfrei probieren. Im Vergleich mit  anderen Tages-Planungs-App‘s hat Tiimo meiner Meinung nach den besten Ansatz. 
Leider ist die technische Umsetzung aktuell so fehlerhaft, dass eine langfristige Nutzung für mich aktuell nicht in Frage kommt. Dazu gehören Punkte wie eine KI, die in meiner Sprache antwortet,  importierte Erinnerungen, die sich nicht bei Import vervielfachen (eigentlich sollten diese Synchronisiert werden, nicht nur importiert), Kalender die korrekt synchronisiert werden (inklusive Wegzeit) und eine Zeitleiste, die ich wirklich per Drag and Drop umstrukturieren kann (ohne dass meine Aufgaben mit einer Startzeit von 00:00 Uhr versehen werden). 
Meiner Meinung nach ist es sehr schade, dass all diese technischen Probleme diese App unbrauchbar machen. Von den Ideen her, mit dem Aufgaben Timer, der lockeren Tagesunterteilung Ohne feste Zeiten und vielen anderen Dingen, ist es nämlich die von vielversprechendste App die ich bisher getestet hab. 
PS: Bitte antwortet nur, wenn Ihr etwas produktives zu sagen habt. Ich benötige keine Antwort, wenn es nur die Standard Antwort von einem Bot ist, der hofft das ich in Zukunft 5 Sterne geben werde.

I’m diagnosed ADHD but this app is not for me - if you are looking for an app to help you organise your day and keep you on track throughout your day, then this may be the app for you, but I can already plan and manage my day without using an app. 
But the main reason for the 1* rating is due to the ridiculous process that you have to go through to cancel your subscription! Hands down the worst experience I’ve ever had canceling anything. It was a very simple 1-click process to sign up, so there’s no excuse for not having the same to cancel - made even worse when you consider how difficult most people with ADHD find cancelling subscriptions! You should all be ashamed of yourselves!

reviews.text: I want to love this app. I’m trying it right now on iPad and iPhone, and while it works OK on iPhone, it’s basically unusable on iPad. All my tasks are just shown as “anytime”, no matter what time of day they’re actually set for. Also, it keeps telling me that I can pinch for week view (seriously, it tells me like every day) and that doesn’t even work! C’mon, don’t spam me about a gesture that doesn’t even work. Also it asks for an app store review way too frequently - well here’s hoping that after this one it’ll stop asking. I also think the core of the service is missing some features that really would make it very useful. I’m not sure why there’s no feature about outstanding todos. That seems like a pretty basic but valuable feature. Overall I’m going to try to stick with this app - like I said, I want to love it - but that will highly depend on whether the iPad app becomes usable and if they start polishing more of the experience. I understand there are probably growing pains right now because of the inevitable influx of new users recently, so I will be patient. But 1 star is unfortunately the current experience in my opinion.

During initial set up there's a stage to add additional tasks, I had no additional tasks but there was no way to skip the stage. I made something up just to get past this point and then got to a daily planner type view, which was just with blank fields, again with no explanation as to how the app worked or what data to fill in. I should not have to work so hard to figure out how to use something that is supposed to be helping me, and then have to pay for the privilege.

reviews.title: Quit shoehorning in bad AI
reviews.text: I downloaded the app after learning it was designed for neurodivergent users. I’ve used Todoist for years and wanted to evaluate how this tool measures up. The primary issue is placement of the AI chatbot. It occupies the lower-right corner of the screen, precisely where the task-creation button should be. The design choice signals a push toward using the chatbot, but it performs poorly. It slows down basic actions, requires far more time than manual entry, and adds no value for simple tasks. Meanwhile, the actual “add task” button is undersized, low-contrast, and difficult to access. For these reasons, I do not intend to continue beyond the trial period.

For something that’s advertised as being great for adhd, there’s many reasons why it’s not adhd friendly at all, and not reminding people with object permanence that a trial is ending is just one of those reasons! A big one, but only one! I highly recommend you don’t sign up for the trial until you’ve done some thorough research on this app, and also remember you need reminders for the reminders cos this worked no different for me than any other calendar, and they’re all bad for adhd!!

reviews.title: Modification nécessaire de l’application pour un réel usage au quotidien
reviews.text:
- temps de tâches plus précis en minutes au minimum (ex: 2minutes brossage de dent, 8minutes de trajet)
- accès à une mise en page calendrier (en + des autres) pour voir les vides dans le planning visuellement
- la fonction schedule doit comprendre des précision (morning, day, night par ex)
- schedule ne doit pas ajouter une tâche là où une autre se trouve
- schedule doit pouvoir programmer une tâche longue sur plusieurs jours
- schedule ne devrait pas ajouter une tâche à n’importe quand, sinon ça n’apporte rien
Pour le moment, cette fonction est inutile.
- il faut pouvoir changer l’ordre des tâches dans matin, jour, soir facilement 
- il faut pouvoir ajouter un groupe (ex midi, nuit, yoga matinal en plus de matin jour et soir) pour permettre de bouger un groupe de tâches facilement 
- recherche d’emojis par le clavier
Si vous vous rapprocher de l’app routinery pour travailler ensemble, vous pourriez faire quelques chose d’intéressant et plus facile à utiliser. Pour le moment l’application n’est pas pratique à utiliser au quotidien.
Il y a de bonnes choses, la synchronisation avec le calendrier, la possibilité d’avoir des actions planifier et d’autres à lancer quand on est prêt, le visuel et le temps automatique. Je comprends que l’app est moins complète que le site web, je vais donc prendre le temps de le tester avant de donner mon avis dessus.
